Main.sentence: Jeremiah Alvesta Wright Jr. (born September 22, 1941) is a ___E:pastor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pastor)___ ___E:emeritus U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emeritus)___ of ___E:Trinity United Church of Christ U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trinity_United_Church_of_Christ)___ in ___E:Chicago U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago)___ , a congregation he led for 36 years, during which its membership grew to over 8,000 parishioners.

Following retirement, his beliefs and preaching were ___E:scrutinized U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeremiah_Wright_controversy)___ when segments of his sermons about ___E:terrorist attacks on the United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/September_11_attacks)___ and government dishonesty were publicized in connection with the ___E:2008 presidential campaign U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_2008_presidential_campaign)___ of ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ .

Wright was born on September 22, 1941.  He was born and raised in the racially mixed area of ___E:Germantown U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germantown,_Philadelphia)___ , ___E:Philadelphia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia)___ , ___E:Pennsylvania U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pennsylvania)___ .

His parents were Jeremiah Wright Sr. (1909–2001), a ___E:Baptist U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baptist)___ minister who pastored Grace Baptist Church in Germantown from 1938 to 1980,  and Mary Elizabeth Henderson Wright, a schoolteacher who was the first Black person to teach an academic subject at Roosevelt Junior High. She went on to be the first Black person to teach at ___E:Germantown High U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germantown_High_School_(Philadelphia))___ and ___E:Girls High U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_High_School_for_Girls)___ , where she became the school's first Black vice principal.

Wright graduated from ___E:Central High School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_High_School_(Philadelphia,_Pennsylvania))___ of Philadelphia in 1959, among the best schools in the area at the time.  At the time, the school was around 90 percent white.

The 211th class yearbook described Wright as a respected member of the class. "Always ready with a kind word, Jerry is one of the most congenial members of the 211," the yearbook said. "His record in Central is a model for lower class [younger] members to emulate."

From 1959 to 1961, Wright attended ___E:Virginia Union University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_Union_University)___ ,  in ___E:Richmond U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richmond,_Virginia)___ and is a member of ___E:Omega Psi Phi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omega_Psi_Phi)___ fraternity, Zeta chapter.

In 1961 Wright left college and joined the ___E:United States Marine Corps U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Marine_Corps)___ and became part of the ___E:2nd Marine Division U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2nd_Marine_Division_(United_States))___ attaining the rank of ___E:private first class U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Private_first_class)___ .

In 1963, after two years of service, Wright joined the ___E:United States Navy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Navy)___ and entered the ___E:Corpsman School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naval_Hospital_Corps_School)___ at the ___E:Great Lakes Naval Training Center U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Lakes_Naval_Training_Center)___ .

Wright was then trained as a ___E:cardiopulmonary U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiopulmonary)___ technician at the ___E:National Naval Medical Center U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Naval_Medical_Center)___ in ___E:Bethesda, Maryland U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bethesda,_Maryland)___ .

Wright was assigned as part of the medical team charged with care of ___E:President U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States)___ ___E:Lyndon B. Johnson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyndon_B._Johnson)___ (see photo of Wright caring for Johnson after his 1966 surgery).

Before leaving the position in 1967, the ___E:White House Physician U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House_Physician)___ , Vice Admiral Burkley, personally wrote Wright a letter of thanks on behalf of the United States President.

In 1967 Wright enrolled at ___E:Howard University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Howard_University)___ in Washington, DC, where he earned a ___E:bachelor's degree U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor%27s_degree)___ in 1968 and a ___E:master's degree U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master%27s_degree)___ in ___E:English U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_studies)___ in 1969. He also earned a ___E:master's degree U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master%27s_degree)___ from the ___E:University of Chicago Divinity School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Chicago_Divinity_School)___ .

Wright holds a ___E:Doctor of Ministry U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_of_Ministry)___ degree (1990) from the ___E:United Theological Seminary U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Theological_Seminary)___ in ___E:Dayton, Ohio U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dayton,_Ohio)___ , where he studied under ___E:Samuel DeWitt Proctor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samuel_DeWitt_Proctor)___ , a mentor to ___E:Martin Luther King Jr. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Luther_King_Jr.)___
Wright and his wife Ramah Reed Wright have four daughters: Janet Marie Moore, Jeri Lynne Wright, Nikol D. Reed, and Jamila Nandi Wright, and one son, Nathan D. Reed.

Wright became pastor of the Trinity United Church of Christ, Chicago on March 1, 1971; it had some 250 members on its rolls, but only about 90 or so were actually attending worship by that time.  By March 2008 Trinity United Church of Christ had become the largest church in the mostly white  ___E:United Church of Christ U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Church_of_Christ)___ denomination.

The President and General Minister of the United Church of Christ, John H. Thomas, has stated: "It is critical that all of us express our gratitude and support to this remarkable congregation, to Jeremiah A. Wright for his leadership over 36 years."  Thomas, who is a member of the Pilgrim Congregational United Church of Christ in ___E:Cleveland U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleveland)___ , has also preached  and worshipped at Trinity United Church of Christ (most recently on March 2, 2008).

Trinity and Wright were profiled by correspondent ___E:Roger Wilkins U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Wilkins)___ in Sherry Jones' documentary Keeping the Faith , broadcast as the June 16, 1987, episode of the ___E:PBS U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_Broadcasting_Service)___ series Frontline with Judy Woodruff .
In 1995, Wright was asked to deliver a prayer during an afternoon session of speeches at the ___E:Million Man March U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Million_Man_March)___ in Washington, DC.

Wright, who began the "Ministers in Training" program at Trinity United Church of Christ, has been a national leader in promoting ___E:theological U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theology)___ education and the preparation of seminarians for the African American church.

The church's mission statement is based upon systematized ___E:black theology U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_theology)___ that started with the works of ___E:James Hal Cone U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Hal_Cone)___ .

Wright has been a professor at ___E:Chicago Theological Seminary U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Theological_Seminary)___ , ___E:Garrett–Evangelical Theological Seminary U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garrett%E2%80%93Evangelical_Theological_Seminary)___ , and other educational institutions.

Wright has served on the Board of Trustees of ___E:Virginia Union University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_Union_University)___ , Chicago Theological Seminary and ___E:City Colleges of Chicago U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_Colleges_of_Chicago)___ .

He has also served on the Board Directors of Evangelical Health Systems, the Black Theology Project, the Center for New Horizons and the Malcolm X School of Nursing, and on boards and committees of other religious and civic organizations.

Wright attended a lecture by Frederick G. Sampson in ___E:Richmond, Virginia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richmond,_Virginia)___ , in the late 1980s, on the ___E:G. F. Watts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G._F._Watts)___ painting Hope , which inspired him to give a sermon in 1990 based on the subject of the painting – "with her clothes in rags, her body scarred and bruised and bleeding, her harp all but destroyed and with only one string left, she had the audacity to make music and praise God....

To take the one string you have left and to have the audacity to hope... that's the real word God will have us hear from this passage and from Watt's painting."  Having attended Wright's sermon, ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ later adapted Wright's phrase "audacity to hope" to "audacity of hope" which became the title for his ___E:2004 Democratic National Convention keynote address U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_Democratic_National_Convention_keynote_address)___ , and the title of his ___E:second book U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Audacity_of_Hope)___ .

Wright, who was Barack Obama's former pastor, gained national attention in March 2008 when ___E:ABC News U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_News_(United_States))___ , after reviewing dozens of Wright's sermons,  excerpted parts which were subject to intense media scrutiny.

Obama denounced the statements in question, but after critics continued to press the issue of his relationship with Wright he gave a speech titled " ___E:A More Perfect Union U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_More_Perfect_Union_(speech))___ ", in which he denounced Wright's remarks, but did not disown him as a person.

The controversy began to fade, but was renewed in late April when Wright made a series of media appearances, including an interview on Bill Moyers Journal , a speech at the ___E:NAACP U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NAACP)___ and a speech at the ___E:National Press Club U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Press_Club_(USA))___ .
After the last of these, Obama spoke more forcefully against his former pastor, saying that he was "outraged" and "saddened" by his behavior, and in May he resigned his membership in the church.

Nearly five months after the late 2008 ___E:Israeli invasion of Gaza resulting in heavy casualties U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_War_(2008%E2%80%932009))___ , on June 9, 2009, in an interview with the Daily Press of Newport News , Wright indicated that he had no contact with Obama up to that point because "Them Jews aren't going to let him talk to me. I told my baby daughter, that he'll talk to me in five years when he's a ___E:lame duck U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lame_duck_(politics))___ , or in eight years when he's out of office." Wright also suggested that Obama did not send a delegation to the ___E:Durban Review Conference U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Durban_Review_Conference)___ in ___E:Geneva U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geneva)___ on racism because of ___E:Zionist U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zionist)___ pressure, saying: "[T]he Jewish vote, the ___E:A-I-P-A-C U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Israel_Public_Affairs_Committee)___ vote, that's controlling him, that would not let him send representation to the Durban Review Conference, that's talking this craziness on this trip, cause they're Zionists, they would not let him talk to someone who calls a spade what it is."  Writing for The Atlantic , ___E:Ta-Nehisi Coates U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ta-Nehisi_Coates)___ characterized Wright's remarks as "crude conspiratorial ___E:antisemitism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antisemitism)___ ."  On June 11, 2009, Wright amended his remarks during an interview with Mark Thompson on his radio program, Make it Plain. "Let me say like ___E:Hillary U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hillary_Clinton)___ , I misspoke.
Let me just say: ___E:Zionists U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zionism)___ ...
I'm not talking about all Jews, all people of ___E:the Jewish faith U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judaism)___ , I'm talking about Zionists."

Wright wrote on his ___E:Facebook U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Facebook)___ page apologizing for his remarks on June 12, 2009. He wrote, "I mis-spoke and I sincerely meant no harm or ill-will to the American Jewish community or the ___E:Obama administration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Obama_administration)___ ...

I have great respect for the Jewish faith and the foundational (and central) part of our Judeo-Christian tradition."  "In other words", ___E:Jeffrey Goldberg U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeffrey_Goldberg)___ inferred, also in The Atlantic , "he regrets speaking plainly instead of deploying a euphemism."  The pro-Israel ___E:Anti-Defamation League U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-Defamation_League)___ released a statement condemning Wright's remarks as "inflammatory and false.
The notions of Jewish control of the ___E:White House U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House)___ in Reverend Wright's statement express classic anti-Semitism in its most vile form."

In June 2011, in a speech at Empowerment Temple in Baltimore, Wright called the ___E:State of Israel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel)___ " ___E:illegal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_law_and_the_Arab%E2%80%93Israeli_conflict)___ " and " ___E:genocidal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethnic_cleansing#Genocide)___ " and insisted, "To equate ___E:Judaism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judaism)___ with the state of Israel is to equate Christianity with [rapper] ___E:Flavor Flav U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flavor_Flav)___ ."
Wright retired as pastor from Trinity United Church of Christ in early 2008. Over the course of his tenure, he brought the church's membership from 87 in 1972 to over 8,000 parishioners.

Trinity United purchased a lot in ___E:Tinley Park U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tinley_Park,_Illinois)___ , a predominantly white Chicago suburb, and built Wright a 10,340-square-foot (961 m 2 ) home valued at $1.6 million.

In September 2016, Wright had a stroke which paralyzed the left side of his body and left him reliant on a wheelchair;  despite the effect on his voice, Wright continues to give sermons on certain occasions.

Wright has received a ___E:Rockefeller Fellowship U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rockefeller_Fellowship)___ and seven ___E:honorary doctorate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honorary_doctorate)___ degrees, including from ___E:Colgate University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colgate_University)___ , ___E:Lincoln University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lincoln_University_(Pennsylvania))___ (in Pennsylvania), ___E:Valparaiso University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valparaiso_University)___ , ___E:United Theological Seminary U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Theological_Seminary)___ , Chicago Theological Seminary, and ___E:Starr King School for the Ministry U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starr_King_School_for_the_Ministry)___ .
Wright was named one of Ebony magazine's top 15 preachers.

He was also awarded the first Carver Medal by ___E:Simpson College U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simpson_College)___ in January 2008, to recognize Wright as "an outstanding individual whose life exemplifies the commitment and vision of the service of ___E:George Washington Carver U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Washington_Carver)___ ".

On May 1, 2008, ___E:Northwestern University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northwestern_University)___ withdrew its invitation for him to receive an honorary doctorate in light of the controversy over his recent remarks.

Wright has written several books and is featured on ___E:Wynton Marsalis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wynton_Marsalis)___ 's album The Majesty of the Blues , where he recites a spoken word piece written by ___E:Stanley Crouch U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Crouch)___ , and on the ___E:Odyssey Channel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hallmark_Channel)___ series Great Preachers .
